parameters.content:
# Claim Checks | WF2 — Telegram Bot

The Claim Checks bot. Commands work with or without # (search, list, dig, update, reports, provide, provide-all, help). Everything else is a conversation: after dig or update the chat stays on that story, and a reasoning model with web search answers the follow-up questions. A conversation is kept only when the user says save, close or wrap up. Only chats in Store Settings (allowed_chats) are answered; their email gets the weekly PDFs.

**Calls:** "WF3 — Research Pipeline" (search, without waiting), "Bot Commands" (the fixed commands), "Story Chat" (open, ask, save, forget).
**Sections:** Telegram Input → Hand-Off → Reply.
**Standalone:** yes, a main workflow with its own Telegram trigger (a dedicated bot: Telegram sends one bot's messages to one n8n only).
**Alerts:** a failed step in "Bot Commands" or "Story Chat" alerts in the main chat (central handler), and the bot still answers "something went wrong, try again".
**Services called:** Telegram (the Claim Checks bot) · Postgres (claim_checks.conversation_messages) · "WF3 — Research Pipeline", "Bot Commands", "Story Chat".

## Telegram Input

Triggered by: Receive Bot Message, every message to the Claim Checks bot.

What it does, step by step:
1. Store Settings: allowed chats with their email, the id of "WF3".
2. Read Command reads the chat, the message and the message it replies to. The command is the first word, with or without a symbol in front (#search, @search, 2search and search are the same). save, close, wrap up, enough, done and forget take "last 2" or "this one only". Anything else is a question.
3. Allowed Chat? ignores any chat that is not in allowed_chats.
4. Route Command: help, search, a fixed command, or the conversation.

## Hand-Off

Triggered by: Route Command, one row per route.

What it does, step by step:
1. help: Send How-To sends the how-to message (Telegram); Pin How-To pins it.
2. search: Build Run Input → Start Research Run (via WF3), without waiting → Reply Started. "WF3" sends the summary and the PDF link here when done.
3. a fixed command: Answer Command (via Bot Commands). When dig or update shows one story, Story Opened? → Open Story Chat (via Story Chat) opens the conversation on it (update also starts "Follow Up Story").
4. a question, save or forget: Talk In Story Chat (via Story Chat).

## Reply (closing step: send to Telegram)

Triggered by: every row of Hand-Off except help.

What it does, step by step:
1. Reformat For Telegram turns the text into Telegram HTML and cuts it into messages under 3,800 characters (a failed step becomes "something went wrong, try again").
2. Send Reply (Telegram); if Telegram refuses the HTML, Send Plain Reply sends the same text without tags.
3. Link Reply To Conversation (Postgres) records which conversation each sent message belongs to, so replying to it later works.

parameters.text: Claim Checks — how to use me I search Reddit, Hacker News and X for a topic (Google Trends adds what people search for right now), check every claim against official and reliable sources, explain each story, and keep every story in an archive you can search later. Commands work with or without # in front. 1. Start a search: search <topic> looks at the last 7 days; add "today" for the last 24 hours. Example: search AI coding agents today 2. Wait about 10 minutes: the summary arrives here with a link to the PDF; 7-day searches also email the PDF. 3. News by date: list shows the stories of the last 7 days. Add dates, one month at most: list 13 October - 21 October 2026, list September 2026, list last 2 weeks. 4. One story in full: dig 214 or dig the AI virus that kills bacteria. 5. What happened since: update 214 did the patient survive? looks for reliable news after the story. 6. Talk about it: after dig or update just ask, e.g. "how did they find out?" or "what does it mean for me?". I search the web and read the sources. 7. Keep it or not: save keeps a summary of the conversation (dig and update use it later); close or enough saves and ends it; save last 2 or save this one only keeps just part. forget or forget last message drops it. A conversation you never save is not remembered. 8. Older conversations: reply to any of their messages with save, forget or a new question. 9. Reports: reports lists the reports of the last 14 days; reply with a number for its summary. provide gives the latest one, provide-all the full briefing of the one you opened last. 10. This message again: help Labels: ✅ Corroborated (2+ independent sources), 🔹 Single source (one official or reliable source so far), ⚠️ Disputed (a trustworthy source says otherwise), ❔ Unverified (nothing trustworthy found), 💬 Opinion (a view, not a checkable fact).

parameters.query:
-- Remembers which conversation each sent message belongs to, so replying to it later saves, forgets or continues that conversation.
INSERT INTO claim_checks.conversation_messages (chat_id, telegram_message_id, conversation_id, exchange_no)
SELECT $1, NULLIF($2, '')::bigint, NULLIF($3, '')::int, coalesce(NULLIF($4, '')::int, 0) WHERE NULLIF($2, '') IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF($3, '') IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (chat_id, telegram_message_id) DO NOTHING;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [String($('Reformat For Telegram').item.json.chat_id), String(($json.result || {}).message_id || ''), String($('Reformat For Telegram').item.json.conversation_id || ''), String($('Reformat For Telegram').item.json.exchange_no || '0')] }}
